title: Hedra Pricing 2026: Plans, Credits and Cost per Video
summary: Hedra pricing starts at $20/month and goes up to $100 depending on your credit allocation. Determine which plan fits your project's usage pattern.
body_markdown:
## What Hedra Plans Cost at Realistic Monthly Usage


At Character-3's 720p rate of[5 cents per second](https://www.hedra.com/models/video/google/veo-3) , a finished minute costs $3.00 before re-renders. **A weekly clip runs about $12 a month** and a daily short about $45.


### Estimate Monthly Hedra Cost From Finished Minutes


Multiply seconds by the per-second rate, because seconds are what Hedra meters. The table below uses my own assumptions: a one-minute weekly clip, ten two-minute explainers a month, and a 30-second daily short.


It prices each at 5 cents per second, so every extra render adds the same amount again.


Use Finished minutes a month Cost per minute at 5¢/s Monthly cost, one render each


Weekly talking-head clip 4 $3.00 $12


Monthly explainer batch 20 $3.00 $60


Daily short 15 $3.00 $45


Nearly as much spend for fewer minutes: that is the daily short set against the explainer batch. That's why a plan chosen by "videos per month" misleads: ten explainers and thirty shorts are different amounts of metered video.


Change the model and the rate moves further than any plan change could. Kling V3 Standard costs[12.6 cents per second](https://www.hedra.com/models/video/google/veo-3) , about $7.56 a minute, roughly 2.5 times Character-3.


Veo 3 Fast is 15 cents ($9.00 a minute), and Kling V3 Pro is 16.8 cents ($10.08), making Kling Pro $1.08 more expensive per minute.


**At 40 cents, or $24 a minute** , Veo 3 Standard would cost $96 for the weekly clip alone, which means additional content segments would substantially increase the total cost. Choosing a premium model for talking heads multiplies the bill, not the quality you need.


### Weekly clips on the lowest paid plan


If its credits cover four finished minutes a month, the lowest paid plan is the natural fit, since that is the smallest workload here.


Test it by doubling the figure. If each clip needs two renders to get a usable take, you're buying eight minutes, about $24 of Character-3 time. A plan that barely clears four minutes will run dry in the second week.


### When to Upgrade Hedra Plans for Batch Explainers


Twenty finished minutes, rendered twice, means 40 minutes of metered video, or $120 at 5 cents per second.


At that volume, compare two numbers: the price gap to the next plan, and what the extra credits would cost if bought separately. If the gap is smaller, upgrade.


Run the same test on the daily short, where 15 minutes doubled is 30. The cheapest plan only stays cheap if you rarely re-render.
